summary: Comprehensive backend (35 pytest cases) + frontend smoke tests for Consentalk. 34/35 backend tests passing (97%). Frontend auth screen, FAQ, Home (mic-orb), Profile, Activity, Transparency all render correctly with seeded session token. One real backend bug found in report risk-score escalation.

minor.issue: Risk-score escalation never transitions through 'restricted' state. Once user.status becomes 'warned', subsequent reports do NOT escalate to 'restricted' at score>=5 because the elif checks `status == 'active'` (a 'warned' user fails this). User goes warned -> warned -> ... -> suspended at score 8, skipping 'restricted'. Fix: change elifs to compare against the full state machine (e.g., allow upgrading from 'warned' to 'restricted' if score>=5).

critical_code_review_comments: Reports escalation state machine only escalates from 'active' for warn/restrict tiers — see backend_issues.minor.
Forensic 'encryption' is base64 obfuscation only (server.py noted as placeholder for libsodium). Acceptable for MVP but should not be marketed as encrypted forensic without real key management.
WebSocket auth uses query-string token; fine for now but token is logged in URL. Consider authenticated WS handshake header in production.
/api/auth/session returns session_token in JSON AND sets httpOnly cookie — the body token is what the web client persists in localStorage, so the httpOnly cookie is largely redundant but harmless.
server.py is 957 lines — close to 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into routers (auth, rooms, admin, forensic) for maintainability.

rca_of_issue: Bug: POST /api/reports — user status never reaches 'restricted'. RCA: in server.py escalation block (lines ~692-699), the elif for score>=5 and elif for score>=3 both gate on `new_status == 'active'`. Once status is 'warned' (set at score 3), all subsequent reports fall through every elif (status != active) until score>=8 where the unconditional 'suspended' branch fires. Reproduction: send 8 reports against a fresh active user — observe statuses progress: active(1)->active(2)->warned(3)->warned(4)->warned(5)->warned(6)->warned(7)->suspended(8). 'restricted' is never reached. Mitigation: change escalation to monotonically take max of current and threshold-derived status, e.g., set new_status to highest applicable tier independent of current status (only special-case 'blacklisted' as terminal).
